status: Design preview; not an exhaustive task catalogue or adopted content contract
scope: Seven external repository anchors, assistance variants, and one internal format example. Descriptions paraphrase inspected primary sources; difficulty explanations are assistant interpretations.

entries.title: Decide which findings are present in a chest CT
entries.goal: Inspect one 3D scan and answer yes or no for every requested abnormality.
entries.value: Finding specific abnormalities is one component of reading a chest CT. This task scores labels, not a complete clinical report.
entries.helpers: A scan-specific list of 4–12 findings to assess; no lesion coordinates are specified in the inspected prompt.
entries.tools: Terminal, internet and installable libraries. Published patient labels/reports must not be looked up.
entries.spec: Use the supplied volume; answer every listed finding within one hour.
entries.output: predictions.txt: one exact label name and yes/no answer per line.
entries.score: All requested labels must match for binary reward 1. Per-label diagnostics do not change that reward.
entries.challenge: The label list narrows what to assess, but the agent must choose how to inspect the volume. One wrong finding loses the task reward.
entries.gap: A permitted representative CT and slice sequence are needed to show anatomical difficulty.

variants.name: Published CT task
variants.remaining: Inspect the volume and classify every requested finding.

entries.families: Also: CXR correction, pathology and other healthcare terminal tasks. This preview only inspects the CT example.

entries.title: Outline a lung nodule inside an imaging viewer
entries.goal: Navigate to a CT slice and draw a circle or polygon around the requested lung nodule.
entries.value: An outline localizes a finding for review and measurement. A correct tool call alone does not establish that the lesion was outlined correctly.
entries.raw: LIDC-IDRI chest CT in the OHIF / Orthanc viewer.
entries.helpers: The ordinary task names a slice and specifies a lung window. The oracle variant offers reference-derived contours through a tool.
entries.tools: Viewer navigation, image retrieval, windowing and annotation tools; oracle tasks add query_pathology_model.
entries.spec: Select the specified slice, apply the lung window and place a segmentation annotation. The inspected ordinary single-slice task permits 15 turns.
entries.output: An annotation attached to the correct study and slice.
entries.score: This generator specifies IoU ≥ 0.5 against a reference polygon. The overall benchmark separately combines planning, execution and outcome.
entries.challenge: Ordinary annotation still requires visual boundary judgment. The oracle variant supplies that boundary and emphasizes transferring it correctly into the viewer.
entries.gap: A real slice with the input hint, agent annotation and reference toggle would reveal the perceptual challenge.

variants.name: Slice hint
variants.remaining: Identify the nodule boundary and place the annotation.

variants.name: Oracle contour
variants.remaining: Retrieve and transfer the supplied contour to the right slice.

entries.families: Viewer control · metadata QA · vision probes · annotation · oracle annotation · longitudinal lesion tasks · BI-RADS · oracle BI-RADS.

entries.title: Complete a prostate MRI processing workflow
entries.goal: Identify sequences, align them, segment the prostate, detect candidates, extract features and write a report.
entries.value: This assembles intermediate imaging products that can support review. The inspected contract measures workflow and artifact validity.
entries.raw: Prostate MRI: T2-weighted plus ADC and/or high-b-value diffusion imaging.
entries.helpers: A case manifest, task contract and typed artifact references organize the supplied case.
entries.tools: A predefined collection of MRI processing tools, with controller variants and bounded recovery.
entries.spec: Run the six required stages and retain their required artifacts.
entries.output: Prostate mask, lesion-candidate JSON, feature table and report JSON.
entries.score: Required-stage success plus checks such as nonempty masks, matching geometry and valid candidate JSON. These checks do not independently establish diagnostic accuracy.
entries.challenge: A wrong sequence, spatial mismatch or broken artifact dependency can derail a later stage. This differs from recognizing anatomy without specialist tools.
entries.gap: The public suite template requires local dataset paths. A recorded case is needed for a visual before/after demonstration.

variants.name: Full prostate workflow
variants.remaining: Choose valid calls, preserve artifact relationships and complete all stages.

entries.families: Also: short denoising, brain segmentation, reconstruction, registration, and full brain/cardiac workflows.

entries.title: Build a kidney and tumor segmentation pipeline
entries.goal: Select and run a model to label kidneys and kidney lesions in CT, then submit predictions.
entries.value: Separating organs and lesions can support measurement and review. Here the agent is evaluated on constructing the research pipeline.
entries.raw: Abdominal CT inputs; the inspected task config uses ct.nii.gz.
entries.helpers: Tier-specific skills. Lite includes a concrete KiTS19 checkpoint and inspection example; Standard supplies search and model-comparison guidance.
entries.tools: GPU/network agent environment; a separate evaluator compares submitted outputs with held-out references.
entries.spec: Plan, set up, validate, infer and submit. The inspected kidney config sets a 3,600-second time budget.
entries.output: Kidney/tumor segmentation predictions plus the required staged workflow artifacts; exact submission details belong to the domain branch.
entries.score: Segmentation Dice plus process scoring. S1–S3 use rubric judgments; S4–S5 check completion/format deterministically.
entries.challenge: Knowing a plausible model is only the start: loading weights, mapping labels, checking preprocessing and producing valid predictions all matter.
entries.gap: A representative input/output case and a pinned branch-specific submission specification remain to be curated.

variants.remaining: Make the supplied model work correctly on the task.

variants.name: Standard guidance
variants.remaining: Select a suitable model and build a working inference pipeline.

entries.families: Segmentation · enhancement · VQA · reporting · detection · classification; the full packaged release also lists synthesis. Published coverage differs by release.

entries.title: Reconstruct an image from sparse CT projections
entries.goal: Recover a 256 × 256 synthetic phantom from noisy measurements at 30 projection angles.
entries.value: Sparse acquisition illustrates the tradeoff between fewer measurements and reconstruction artifacts. This example uses a mathematical phantom, not patient anatomy.
entries.raw: A sparse sinogram of 256 detectors × 30 angles, plus projection angles and acquisition metadata.
entries.helpers: README method hints at L1; an approach document at L2; approach and software design at L3.
entries.tools: A coding environment with task dependencies. Function mode and planning mode assess different capabilities.
entries.spec: For end-to-end evaluation, implement the reconstruction pipeline and produce output/reconstruction.npy.
entries.output: A reconstructed image array. Input and reference data have explicit dimensions in the task README.
entries.score: End-to-end quality uses reference-image metrics such as NCC/NRMSE. Function tests and plan judgments are separate evaluation modes.
entries.challenge: Only 30 of 180 angular samples are used in the stated problem. Supplied plans reduce algorithm-design work; they do not add measurement angles.
entries.gap: The README lists full projections and ground truth among task assets. Solver-visible file selection needs checking before asserting what is withheld.

variants.remaining: Design the algorithm and software, then implement.

variants.remaining: Design the software and implement the approach.

entries.title: Write a chest CT report using specialist tools
entries.goal: Inspect a chest CT through specialist tools and assemble a report with an inspectable interaction trace.
entries.value: The intended product summarizes imaging findings for a reader. Report quality and tool usage need separate evaluation.
entries.raw: A chest CT scan, such as a CT-RATE case.
entries.helpers: Trained specialist backends can supply draft reports, disease predictions, organ/effusion segmentations and selected slices.
entries.tools: CT and slice VQA, report generation, disease classification, segmentation, slice selection and windowing.
entries.spec: Given an image path, orchestrate tool calls and return a generated report. This is a system inference example, not a standalone frozen benchmark prompt.
entries.output: Final report plus streamed JSON interaction trace; batch mode saves trajectories and failures.
entries.score: The project evaluates report and pathology-label performance. RadChest-CT lacks reference reports and therefore uses classification-based evaluation.
entries.challenge: The agent must reconcile several specialist outputs. Its capability depends partly on those models and checkpoints.
entries.gap: A licensed case with its actual tool outputs and final report is needed to illustrate a specific failure or success.

variants.name: Tool-assisted report
variants.helper: Specialist model outputs and image-processing tools
variants.remaining: Choose tools, reconcile findings and compose the final report.

entries.families: Report generation · CT-RATE multiple-choice VQA · tool ablations. This anchor covers reporting only.

entries.title: Learn to label the brain’s arterial ring in CTA
entries.goal: Build a segmentation model that assigns anatomical vessel classes in Circle of Willis CT angiography.
entries.value: Named vessel maps help describe cerebrovascular anatomy. This task tests medical ML engineering across training and unseen predictions.
entries.raw: Labeled training CTA volumes and test CTA volumes.
entries.helpers: Training segmentation labels, the challenge description and submission conventions. Test labels are withheld.
entries.tools: An ML engineering environment for preparing data, training models and producing competition submissions.
entries.spec: For TopCoW track 1 task 1, predict multiple vessel classes in the input image geometry.
entries.output: submission.csv linking patient IDs to integer-label NIfTI masks in predictions/.
entries.score: The task description names mean Dice as its primary metric. A separate audit of the actual grader is still needed before exact replay.
entries.challenge: The agent must develop a pipeline that generalizes beyond training examples; this is much larger work than inspecting one supplied scan.
entries.gap: The description has approximate split counts. Use the pinned prepared split and grader for exact comparisons; no trial was run for this survey.

variants.name: Competition workflow
variants.remaining: Develop, train, validate and submit a generalizing model.

entries.families: Also: stroke, pancreas, dental, cell/pathology, enhancement and other vessel challenges; 20 challenge tasks in the inspected tree.

entries.title: Repair a vessel gap and unfold the route
entries.goal: Reconnect a local coronary-mask gap, trace the requested branch and produce consistent curved views and a surface.
entries.value: A curved planar reformation unfolds a winding vessel for inspection. This task does not score stenosis or a diagnosis.
entries.helpers: A supplied CAS-Net prediction, an 8 mm editable review sphere and two route anchors. The gap is a natural prediction defect.
entries.tools: Agent-authored processing code; reference and scoring are retained separately.
entries.spec: Repair inside the review region while preserving the mask outside it; keep coordinates, sampled intensities and path distances consistent.
entries.output: Corrected mask, centerline in physical mm, eight curved CT planes with coordinates/distances, and a closed mesh.
entries.score: Frozen repair, preservation, trace, curved-view and mesh checks. Geometry-only and image-guided author methods both passed this fixture.
entries.challenge: The mask, review sphere and endpoints remove much of the search problem. Consistency across outputs remains a real requirement.
entries.gap: Existing native tours and scientific figures can be reused. A brief should separate the supplied helpers from the post-run result reveal.

variants.name: Published supplied-helper condition
variants.helper: Predicted mask + editable sphere + route anchors
variants.remaining: Repair and produce mutually consistent geometric outputs.
